_meta.purpose: Blocking news events. An event appears in the inbox and the turn CANNOT be advanced until it is resolved — unlike policy cards, which may be ignored. This is what makes consequences feel imposed rather than shopped for.

triggers.afterOption: Fires N quarters after a specific card option was enacted. Consequence chains.
triggers.flag: Fires when a flag is set.
triggers.threshold: Fires when a state variable crosses a value.

_meta.note: Options carry opinion deltas directly, since events are where relationships actually move between turns.
_meta.scripted: Events with a scriptedQuarter fire on that quarter of the run regardless of player action. These are the things that were already happening in 2026 — the Hormuz closure, the Constitutional Court petition, the baht/tourism row. The player inherits them.
_meta.fail_states: Two events now carry real jeopardy. forced_consolidation fires above 79% of GDP and takes spending out of the player's hands. confidence_crisis fires below 31% approval and can end the run outright if the player calls a bluff that was not one.

events.headline: Southern provinces erupt over Land Bridge land seizures
events.body: Expropriation notices in Ranong and Chumphon have brought thousands onto the streets. Fishing communities say the deep-sea port will kill their livelihoods; the environmental review is still in court. The People's Party has tabled an urgent debate. Your Transport Minister wants to press on. Interior asks if the police will clear the sites.

options.label: Force it through
options.body: Clear the sites, issue the construction notice. No going back.
options.flavour: You own every photograph taken in Ranong for six years.

options.label: Pull back — build the rail link instead
options.body: Cancel the ports, keep the corridor, recover some of the committed capital.
options.flavour: Looks competent to everyone except those promised a trillion baht.

events.headline: Civil service unions call coordinated slowdown
events.body: Provincial offices are processing permits at a crawl. Nothing is technically a strike. The Office of the Civil Service Commission says the early-retirement terms are misrepresented; the unions say 414,000 people are being pushed out at forty with a lump sum and a reskilling leaflet. Disbursement has stalled in eleven ministries.

options.label: Improve the severance terms
options.body: Better package, faster uptake, bigger bill.
options.flavour: You bought back the bureaucracy at its asking price.

options.label: Hold the line
options.body: No renegotiation. Slowdown runs two more quarters.
options.flavour: Execution collapses short term. Survive it and the reform survives.

options.label: Exempt frontline services
options.body: Teachers, health and police carved out. Two thirds of the saving, a third of the fight.
options.flavour: Survivable. It will not reach 1.35 million.

events.headline: VAT rise triggers largest protests since 2020
events.body: Three percentage points overnight, on everything, five months after deflation. Bangkok is blocked. The opposition has a slogan. Your backbenches are sweating.

options.label: Hold the rate
options.flavour: The revenue is real and so is the anger.

options.label: Add a low-income rebate
options.flavour: Gives back a quarter of what you took from the poorest quarter.

options.label: Phase it after all
options.flavour: Spent the political capital, kept half the revenue.

events.headline: Concessionaire files for international arbitration
events.body: Asia Era One wants compensation well above the 12 billion baht it says it spent. Foreign chambers of commerce have written jointly to the Prime Minister's Office. The Board of Investment says three unrelated concession enquiries have gone silent.

options.label: Settle quickly
options.flavour: Expensive. Stops the bleeding on every other concession.

options.label: Contest it
options.flavour: Popular at home. Every infrastructure investor in Asia is reading the filing.

events.headline: Global energy prices spike: fuel and transport costs surge
events.body: Headline inflation moves this month whatever you do. Energy passes into headline CPI at over four times the rate it reaches core, and fuel prices are what voters notice.

options.label: Cap retail fuel prices
options.flavour: Instant relief, permanent expectation. Thailand has never unwound one cleanly.

options.label: Targeted transport subsidy only
options.flavour: A third of the cost, a third of the credit.

options.label: Let prices pass through
options.flavour: Correct, cheap, and how governments lose by-elections.

events.headline: Fiscal Policy Office warns debt ceiling will be breached
events.body: Gross public debt is within 1.5 points of the statutory ceiling. The Fiscal Policy Office has written formally. Rating agencies have not moved, but two want a meeting.

options.label: Legislate a higher ceiling — 70% to 78%
options.flavour: Eight points of headroom. No lower risk premium. The next government inherits a meaningless number.

options.label: Cut spending to stay under
options.flavour: Capital is the easiest line to cut and the costliest to lose.

options.label: Note the warning and proceed
options.flavour: Nothing happens yet.

events.headline: Strait of Hormuz closed — fuel imports at risk
events.body: About half of Thailand's crude and a third of its LNG transit Hormuz. Panic buying has pushed daily consumption from 67 to 84 million litres. The Federation of Thai Industries warns heavy-industry costs could rise 50%. Headline CPI, negative three months ago, is about to jump.

options.label: Co-payment fuel credits (2,000–2,400 baht)
options.body: Digital wallet credits for fuel and transport, as drafted.
options.flavour: Fast, popular, and the expectation never goes away.

options.label: Release strategic reserves, cap refinery margins
options.body: No cash out the door. Squeeze the refiners.
options.flavour: Cheaper for the budget. The energy sector will remember.

options.label: Let it pass through
options.body: Prices move. Nothing is spent.
options.flavour: Correct. Every headline will say you did nothing.

events.headline: Constitutional Court accepts petition against the February election
events.body: The Court has voted 6–3 to hear a challenge to the February 8 election. Barcodes and QR codes on ballots could trace voters, the petition says, breaching ballot secrecy. A ruling against the Election Commission could annul the result. Nine judges now hold your mandate.

options.label: Defend the Election Commission publicly
options.flavour: Ties you to an institution the petitioners want discredited.

options.label: Concede the point, legislate ballot reform
options.flavour: Cheap, popular with people who will never vote for you, and an admission the election was flawed.

options.label: Say nothing and govern
options.flavour: Every investment decision is provisional for two quarters.

events.headline: Tourism industry demands the BOT weaken the baht
events.body: ATTA projects 39 million arrivals this year on a Chinese recovery, but not at this exchange rate. A yuan buys about 4.4 baht, down from 5.4. ATTA wants the BOT to target 40 to the dollar, or at least 2019's 35. January arrivals fell 18%. Services exports are 13.2% of GDP.

options.label: Publicly press the BOT to intervene
options.flavour: The Bank will resent it and may ignore it. Investors still price in its independence.

options.label: Fund a tourism marketing and subsidy push instead
options.flavour: Treats the symptom. The hotels are grateful for a season.

options.label: Decline — the rate is not the government's to set
options.flavour: Institutionally correct. The Andaman hotel association has your Transport Minister's number.

events.headline: Bond auction undersubscribed: Treasury forces cuts
events.body: A ten-year auction left a third of the book unfilled. Debt is compounding faster than nominal GDP, and the Public Debt Management Office cannot fund the programme at any acceptable price. You are nine points past the ceiling. Something gets cut this quarter.

options.label: Cut the capital programme
options.flavour: Easiest to cut, costliest to lose. Every project slips a year.

options.label: Cut transfers and subsidies
options.flavour: Saves the investment programme. The people losing transfers notice at once.

options.label: Sell state enterprise stakes
options.flavour: One-off money. The people who ran those enterprises remember.

events.headline: Coalition partner threatens to withdraw
events.body: Approval is low enough that your partners are asked daily why they stay. Their withdrawal would drop the coalition below 251 and end it. Their price: portfolios, a policy concession, or ending the unpopular programme.

options.label: Hand over two ministries
options.flavour: They stay. You traded the agenda for the office.

options.label: Abandon the unpopular programme
options.flavour: Four years of legislation stops being enforced.

options.label: Call their bluff
options.flavour: If they walk, the government falls and the run ends. If not, the threat never returns.
options.body: No concession. The threat is tested.

events.headline: Cabinet has the MOU 2544 termination instrument on the table
events.body: The 2001 memorandum froze the Overlapping Claims Area for 25 years: 26,000 square kilometres of Gulf seabed holding an estimated 10 trillion baht of gas. After the border fighting, the politics are settled. Termination sends the dispute to UNCLOS conciliation and ends joint development.

options.label: Terminate the memorandum
options.body: Instrument signed. The dispute goes to international law.
options.flavour: Popular and sovereign. It kills the only framework that could have got the gas out.

options.label: Retain the memorandum
options.flavour: Are you all right?

events.headline: Fourth revision of the Bangkok comprehensive plan takes effect
events.body: The 2013 master plan expires. Its replacement rezones electric-rail corridors for denser mixed use, with floor-area bonuses near stations. City Hall wrote it, the ministry signed it. The effect reaches your numbers through construction over several years.

options.label: Note the plan and let the pipeline run
options.body: The plan is gazetted. Developers redraw sites along the rail lines.
options.flavour: Property stocks rally. The floor space takes most of a decade to build.

events.headline: Map Ta Phut Phase 3 hands over Stage 1
events.body: Stage 1 of Map Ta Phut Phase 3 is done: reclaimed land and marine works for the gas and petrochemical berths in the Eastern Economic Corridor. It was tendered years before you took office. You cut the ribbon.

options.label: Attend the handover
options.body: Stage 1 accepted. Terminal construction continues on top.
options.flavour: An on-schedule EEC delivery you had nothing to do with. Take the photograph anyway.

events.headline: Laem Chabang Phase 3 opens Wharf F
events.body: Wharf F, Laem Chabang Phase 3's industrial-goods berth, opens. It is the first revenue-earning piece of an expansion that has slipped repeatedly since the concession was signed. Capacity at the main gateway steps up.

options.label: Open the wharf
options.body: Wharf F is running. The Port Authority publishes new throughput targets.
options.flavour: Logistics costs per container dip. Exporters notice; voters do not.

events.headline: MRT Orange Line eastern section enters commercial service
events.body: Thailand Cultural Centre to Minburi opens after test running through late 2027. The western half is years away, so the line stops where the western-contract litigation began.

options.label: Open the line
options.body: First fare-paying passengers on the eastern section.
options.flavour: Minburi finally gets its train. Ridership on half a line will disappoint, and you will get the blame.

events.headline: MRT Purple Line southern extension opens
events.body: Tao Poon to Rat Burana enters service, taking the Purple Line through the old city and across the river. It closes a gap that has forced a bus transfer for years.

options.label: Open the extension
options.body: Through service from Khlong Bang Phai to Rat Burana begins.
options.flavour: Someone's commute improves the day it opens.

events.headline: MRT Orange Line western section completes the corridor
events.body: Bang Khunnon to Thailand Cultural Centre opens, joining the two halves. Bangkok gets its first continuous east-west heavy rail spine, a decade and one Supreme Administrative Court case after approval.

options.label: Complete the corridor
options.body: The full Orange Line runs end to end.
options.flavour: Your last big ribbon, and clearly your predecessors'. Ridership finally makes sense with both halves running.

events.headline: Thailand is asked to sign: Pax Silica, WAICO, or neither
events.body: Washington's Pax Silica declaration has grown from seven signatories to more than two dozen in a year: chips, rare earths, energy, routed around China. Beijing answered in July with WAICO, an AI governance treaty with thirty founding members. Thailand's two largest trading partners sit on opposite lists. The foreign ministry wants a decision before the ASEAN summit.

options.label: Sign Pax Silica
options.body: Thailand signs. Advanced chip access and the data-centre pipeline come with it.
options.flavour: Hyperscalers can site compute here without an export-licence fight. Chinese EV and electronics investment in the EEC, the largest source of new FDI since 2023, takes note.

options.label: Join WAICO
options.body: Thailand accedes to the WAICO treaty and its governance framework.
options.flavour: Chinese capital for grid and data centres arrives fast and cheap. The frontier accelerators do not.

options.label: Stay out of both
options.body: Thailand signs neither and keeps the door open.
options.flavour: It has worked for two centuries. Nobody builds a fab in a country that has not chosen.

options.label: Chart a sovereign AI course
options.body: A national compute programme, a Thai foundation model and a domestic data-sovereignty regime.
options.flavour: Magnificent on the podium. A sovereign model trained on chips you cannot buy is a subsidy to the electricity bill.

events.headline: The 14th National Plan carries the energy transition
events.body: The 14th National Economic and Social Development Plan (2028–2032) carries a hard number: 51% renewable generation by 2037, falling gas, firm-capacity procurement, a small modular reactor study and the grid rebuild it all needs. NESDC has drafted it. Cabinet decides how much to fund.

options.label: Fund the transition in full
options.body: The plan is adopted with the grid and procurement programme fully funded.
options.flavour: Transmission and storage are the real constraint, and this is the window to build them. The return lands two governments from now.

options.label: Adopt the plan, fund the first tranche
options.body: Targets adopted; the grid programme is funded to 2030, then reviewed.
options.flavour: Fiscally defensible. But half a grid connects nothing, and the review falls to a successor.

events.headline: The National Semiconductor Board wants a decision and a budget
events.body: The board has existed since October 2024, chaired by the prime minister: you. Its roadmap: 500 billion baht of foreign investment and 86,000 engineers and scientists in five years. Thailand does only assembly, test and packaging, with no wafer fabrication. Fund it, or let it meet.

options.label: Chair it yourself and fund the secretariat
options.body: The board becomes a standing cabinet priority with a budget line and a workforce programme.
options.flavour: Engineers take six years to train. You have four. Someone else collects.

options.label: Let the board meet and see
options.body: The committee continues on its existing footing.
options.flavour: A roadmap, a launch event and targets nobody owns. It costs nothing, which is why it always happens.

events.headline: EGAT wants a ruling on data-centre power as requests pass 850 MW
events.body: USD 16 billion of data-centre commitments across 28 projects in half a year: AWS 5 billion through 2037, TikTok 3.8 across three provinces, Google 1 in Chonburi, a 300 MW campus in Rayong. Installed capacity is about 200 MW; the pipeline needs 850 MW within three years. Where does firm clean power come from, and at what tariff?

options.label: Guarantee firm clean power and build transmission
options.body: A dedicated tariff and transmission programme for the digital corridor.
options.flavour: The investment is real; the jobs are a few hundred. But a poured data centre cannot be relocated.

options.label: Let them queue for a standard connection
options.body: No dedicated programme. Projects connect as capacity becomes available.
options.flavour: Households should not subsidise the world's largest companies. Johor and Batam already built theirs, and site decisions expire in about eighteen months.

events.headline: U-Tapao Phase 1 opens at a quarter of the promised size
events.body: Construction began in April 2026 under a fifty-year concession, five years late, after the link to the unfinished three-airport rail line was waived. Runway 2 came from the Navy in 2028. Phase 1 shrank from 12–15 million passengers a year to 3–4: 10 billion baht of a 290-billion-baht programme. The Eastern Aviation City is unbuilt.

options.label: Fund the terminal to the original specification
options.body: Cabinet funds the terminal expansion and aviation-city groundworks.
options.flavour: The EEC case needs the aviation city, and the aviation city needs a bigger terminal. Or it is Suvarnabhumi's second runway argument again.

options.label: Open at reduced scope, review in five years
options.body: Phase 1 opens as built. Expansion is deferred to a later review.
options.flavour: Three million passengers is what the routes support, and the concessionaire carries the risk. The Eastern Aviation City stays a rendering.

events.headline: Expo 2029 Korat opens in Khong district
events.body: The International Horticultural Exposition, Category A1 (AIPH and BIE), runs 110 days from 10 November to the end of February. Cabinet approved about 6.7 billion baht; the theme is 'Nature and Greenery'. Thailand's first since Royal Flora Ratchaphruek in 2006, and in the Northeast, where your seats are.

options.label: Open the exposition
options.body: The expo runs to the end of February 2030, through the election.
options.flavour: 6.7 billion baht of horticulture, closing four weeks before the vote. Pure coincidence.

events.headline: Power Development Plan
events.body: Four supply scenarios for 2026–2050 disagree on gas, solar, wind and whether carbon capture is costed. All carry Thailand's first 300 MW small modular reactor in 2037 and about 9,000 MW nuclear by 2050. No new gas plants this decade: turbines have a five-year queue. The National Energy Policy Council wants an answer by year's end.

options.label: Adopt the base case: gas-led transition
options.body: Gas 24,500 MW, solar 28,890 MW, wind 10,360 MW. 65% clean by 2050, 35% fossil.
options.flavour: Cheapest tariff, fewest fights. It keeps 35% fossil to 2050 and assumes uncosted carbon capture covers it.

options.label: Adopt the base case, with carbon capture costed in
options.body: Same fuel mix, with CCS priced into fossil generation.
options.flavour: If capture defends the fossil share, it belongs in the tariff. Voters see that bill monthly, for unproven technology.

options.label: Take the renewables pathway: 89% clean by 2050
options.body: Gas cut to 16,800 MW, solar to 61,300 MW, wind to 52,700 MW, 220,000 MWh of storage, no CCS.
options.flavour: The only net-zero path without unproven technology. Five times Thailand's wind ever built, and every generator will fight it.

options.label: Take the middle path: domestic gas, capture, renewables
options.body: Gas 18,900 MW leaning on the Gulf and Myanmar imports, solar 40,890 MW, wind 23,360 MW. 73% clean.
options.flavour: Strongest energy security, weakest climate case. A quarter of the 2050 grid rests on declining Gulf fields and a twice-closed border.

events.headline: They are coming
events.body:
The prosecution service has been able to open a file without a police referral for one quarter. The first files are not about the opposition. They are about provincial members of your own party, the contractors who fund them, and two people who were in the room when this coalition was assembled.

Nobody has telephoned. Nobody has written anything down. The Secretary-General cleared his afternoon without being asked and will not say why. Three provincial chairmen flew into Bangkok this morning on three separate flights. The chief whip of your own parliamentary party has stopped answering.

They will be in the outer office within the hour, and they will ask you one question.

Are the files going to be withdrawn?

options.label: I will, I will — this was never aimed at you
options.body: The mandate is narrowed. The files come back.
options.flavour:
No — no, listen to me, this was never about any of you. There has been an overreach at the agency, obviously there has, and it will be corrected. I will correct it. The mandate was drafted too broadly, everybody accepts that now, we all said so at the time. We narrow the mandate, the files come back, and none of this ever has to reach a newspaper. You built this party. Nobody in this room is forgetting who built this party.

It works. They go back to work. The Act stays on the books and the whole country now knows exactly what it is worth.

options.label: No.
options.body: The files proceed. The organisation that delivers your seats will not forget this.
options.lockedNote: You are not in a position to say it.
options.flavour: Oh my God.

events.headline: The debt ceiling is reached again
events.body: Gross debt is within a point of the 78% ceiling this cabinet set two years ago. The Fiscal Policy Office has written again, harder. Both rating agencies have scheduled meetings. Their question is the pattern: a limit moved every time it is reached is not a limit.

options.label: Legislate again — 78% to 85%
options.body: Seven more points of headroom. The line stops meaning anything.
options.flavour: The first raise moved a number. The second proves the number moves. State and corporate borrowing reprices against that.

options.label: Emergency consolidation, no second raise
options.body: Capital programmes stopped mid-flight. Transfers cut. The limit holds.
options.flavour: The most painful option, and the only one that keeps the limit real. Half-built projects die first. The political cost lands inside your term.

options.label: Do nothing and go through it
options.body: No legislation, no cuts. The debt passes the ceiling.
options.flavour: The worst option and the easiest. Lenders learn the ceiling was never real.

events.headline: The Tsunami
events.body:
They resigned together in the morning, with a joint letter about conscience. Two are under investigation; four more expect to be. By afternoon eleven had been photographed at another party's headquarters.

They keep their seats. They were never really yours.

options.label: Accept the resignations
options.flavour: They belonged to the provincial machine, not the letterhead. Every remaining vote in this parliament just changed.

events.headline: Off the Cliff
events.body: Ten more, including two deputy chief whips, the people who counted the votes you no longer have. This wave waited a quarter to see whether you would climb down.

options.label: Get out.
options.flavour: The second wave is worse. These are not the implicated; they read which way it is going.

options.label: Get the opposition on the line NOW
options.lockedNote: Requires the People's Party to cross the threshold for you. They will not.
options.flavour: The enemy of my enemy is my friend.

events.headline: All Alone
events.body: Thirty-five more members leave in one morning. The provincial organisation has decided, in public, that it no longer serves the party it built.

options.label: Expel them!
options.flavour: The organisation takes its name off the door and the furniture with it.

events.headline: Screw you
events.body:
A petition reaches the Constitutional Court: dissolve Bhumjaithai and ban its executive committee for ten years, over a 2023 donation declared, audited and signed off at the time.

The petitioner is a nobody. Everyone knows who pays the lawyers.

This is how Thai parties die.

options.label: Unleash our power
options.flavour: Dismissed unanimously, by a court whose independence you legislated eighteen months ago. It still cost two quarters, most of a legal budget, and a stalled bureaucracy.

events.headline: All eyes on you
events.body:
The polling moved after the ruling and stayed. Nobody changed their mind on the Land Bridge, taxes or prices. The question was whether the people running the country are the ones elected to run it.

The provincial networks are gone. What replaced them is rarer.

options.label: We won.
options.flavour: People vote for the party for what it did, not for who asked them to.
